### Unlimited Forgiveness
Author: Ligonier Ministries
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/devotionals/unlimited-forgiveness
Passage: Matthew 18:35
Points:
- Peter believed forgiving someone seven times was generous, but Jesus commanded limitless forgiveness.
- The astronomical debt owed by the servant was impossible to repay and could only be erased by royal grace.
- Christians who have received God's unmerited mercy must reflect that same mercy toward those who wrong them.
- Harboring an unmerciful spirit suggests that one has never truly understood or received God's pardon.
- Daily Christian discipleship requires making the forgiveness of offenses a continuous, habitual practice.

### When You Are the Offended, Part 1
Author: Charles R. Swindoll
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/todays-insight-chuck-swindoll/today-s-insight-february-21-2014.html
Passage: Matthew 18:21-35
Points:
- Peter thought he was being magnanimous by offering seven pardons, but Jesus indicated an infinite standard.
- The master canceling an impossible debt portrays God's lavish vertical forgiveness toward sinners.
- The servant displayed astonishing cruelty by violently demanding payment for a tiny debt right after being forgiven.
- Demanding strict justice from fellow sinners while clinging to God's mercy is pure hypocrisy.

### The Beauty in Forgiveness (Matthew 18:21-22)
Author: Betsy St. Amant Haddox
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/your-daily-bible-verse/your-daily-bible-verse-december-18.html
Passage: Matthew 18:21-22
Points:
- Peter focused on legal minimums when asking his question, but Jesus directed him toward boundless grace.
- Extending continuous forgiveness does not mean submitting to abuse or acting as a doormat.
- Refusing to forgive a repentant fellow believer implicitly suggests the cross was insufficient for that sin.
- Forgiving unbelievers surrenders retribution to God's righteous judgment and witnesses to the gospel.

### Seventy-Seven
Author: Ryan Duncan
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/crosswalk-devo/crosswalk-the-devotional-may-10-2013.html
Passage: Matthew 18:21-22
Points:
- Disagreements and bitter grudges can easily infect Christian relationships and damage communities.
- Jesus made clear that disciples must not keep running tallies of offenses or establish ceilings on mercy.
- The parable illustrates how grievous it is to withhold forgiveness over small matters after being spared total ruin.
- Believers are commanded to forgive others from the heart because God showed them boundless love first.
